sections.h2: Which office records Kent County deeds?
sections.html:
The building is at 300 Monroe Avenue NW, in the middle of downtown. Land contracts, liens and mortgages go through the same counter, under the Michigan Recording Act.

The office is careful about what it will not do. It does not supply blank deeds and it does not advise on how to prepare one. Anyone changing names on a deed can use a real property attorney, a title company or a blank form they fill in. It cautions that forms pulled from the internet may fall short of recording rules.

sections.h2: Why does the Kent County register of deeds see so many transfers?
sections.html:
Kent County is big. The county holds, by the July 2025 Census estimate, 675,232 people and 275,076 housing units across roughly 849 square miles of land. Records here start in 1836, the year the county was organized after being set off from Kalamazoo County in 1831.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 70.3%
  • Home value at the median: $289,900
  • Building permits in 2025: 2,398
  • People in the same house one year earlier: 87.9%

The Grand River runs through the county, and the land rises to 1,048 feet at Fisk Knob Park in Solon Township, so parcels range from river-valley city lots to rolling township acreage. All of them are recorded at one counter. Sellers should have the paperwork squared away before closing.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Kent County?
sections.html:
The base fee is $30 per document, and it has been in place since October 1, 2016. It covers deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and certified copies. The same fee schedule lists the add-ons you are most likely to meet when a house changes hands:

  • Assignments or discharges that cover several instruments add $3 per extra instrument, and the office asks you to limit these to 25 per document.
  • Deeds with a covenant of warranty, plus land contracts, need the treasurer's certification at $5 per deed (up to 25 parcels, 25 cents each beyond that). Write that check to the Kent County Treasurer, not the Register.
  • Copies are $1 per page. Searches start at $5, and certifying a document adds $5.
  • Pay with cash, a check or a money order. The check is written to the Kent County Register of Deeds.

Electronic filers pay the statutory recording fee to the county, and any e-recording vendor can add its own processing fee on top.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies to a Kent County sale?
sections.html:
Add the two posted rates, $1.10 for the county and $7.50 for the state, and every $1,000 of price carries $8.60. Both come straight from Michigan's two transfer tax acts, MCL 207.504 and MCL 207.525.

Transfer tax on sample Kent County sale prices at the posted rates
Sale priceCounty taxState taxTotal
$150,000$165$1,125$1,290
$290,000$319$2,175$2,494
$400,000$440$3,000$3,440

The $290,000 row is near the Census median home value for Kent County, $289,900. The statute taxes each $500 or fraction of $500, so an odd price rounds the count up. There is no transfer tax on mortgages in Michigan.

sections.h2: Where does a Kent County deed get its tax certification?
sections.html:
That stamp comes from the Treasurer's Office, a separate counter from the Register of Deeds. Deed certifications are one of the few transactions the treasurer still takes in person, at the first-floor counter of the Administration Building during weekday business hours, 8 am to 5 pm.

Plan the order of events around that. A seller who learns at the last minute that taxes are open must first pay the treasurer, then collect the certification, and only after that bring the deed to the recording counter. The county's online delinquent tax search lets you check a parcel before you start, and the payment options page covers e-check, card, phone and mail payments for any balance.

sections.h2: Who owes the transfer tax, and how is an exemption claimed?
sections.html:
The seller, or grantor, owes it. Write the full price into the deed, or attach a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit. No fee applies to the affidavit so long as the deed mentions it.

Exemptions must be written on the deed itself. The state's list in MCL 207.526 includes a parent deeding to a child or grandchild, foreclosure deeds, land contracts that have not yet passed title, and court orders that set no price. If land lies in two counties, state the price for each part.

sections.h2: Can you get any of the state transfer tax back?
sections.html:
Possibly, for a seller who held a principal residence exemption and sold at a price close to the property's earlier assessed value. MCL 207.526(u) exempts a conveyance of property that carried the principal residence exemption when the state equalized value is no higher than the value set at the first tax day after the home was built or acquired, and the sale was an arm's-length price.

Kent County's transfer tax page lists what a refund claim needs: the state refund application, copies of the recorded deeds showing the transfer tax stamp and proof of the sales price, and proof of the SEV from the local municipality. Copies of deeds come from the online deed search or from the office itself.

sections.h2: Can a deed be recorded electronically in Kent County?
sections.html:
Yes, through approved e-recording vendors, within a fixed window. Electronic documents are processed on weekdays between 8 am and 5 pm, skipping county holidays, and the fee is collected by ACH through the vendors.

Kent reserves the right to reject any electronic filing that fails the Michigan Recording Act, and a party whose documents violate the state standards is cut off until further notice. The county lists CSC eRecording, ePN, Simplifile and File and Go as the vendors it works with, and each vendor sets its own pricing. Recorded documents return to the submitter in electronic form. An individual seller will usually leave this step to the closing office.

sections.h2: What should a Kent County seller settle before the deed goes in?
sections.html:
Settle the property tax first, because the register of deeds cannot take a warranty deed without a treasurer's certificate. Under MCL 211.135 the certificate depends on a clean five-year tax record. Any open balance is settled by closing, and the Kent County Treasurer will quote it.

Check that the names on the deed match the owners of record. If a parcel's owner is unknown, the office suggests asking Equalization or the local assessor for the tax roll name, which may not match the true owner, and then searching recorded documents under it. After recording, the buyer has 45 days to give the local assessor the transfer notice under MCL 211.27a.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a deed in Kent County?
faqs.a: Recording is $30 a document, under a schedule dated October 1, 2016. Budget a further $5 for the treasurer's tax certification on a warranty deed, plus any vendor charge if a filer submits electronically.

faqs.q: How high is the Kent County transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is $8.60 per $1,000 of price in total, split $1.10 county and $7.50 state. A $250,000 sale produces $2,150, owed by the seller unless the deed states an exemption.

faqs.q: Does the Kent County Register of Deeds help write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office does not supply blank deeds or offer advice on preparing them. It sends people to an attorney, a title company or a blank form.

faqs.q: Will Kent County take a warranty deed while taxes are delinquent?
faqs.a: Not a warranty deed. State law requires a treasurer's certificate that taxes for the previous five years are paid. Quitclaim deeds with no warranty covenants are excepted.

faqs.q: How do I order a certified copy from Kent County?
faqs.a: Visit the office in person, by letter, or through its online document search. Copies cost $1 per page, certification is $5 per document, and a records search carries a $5 minimum.
